item.title: Fiji suffers 8-1 defeat to Senegal in U17 Futsal Youth Olympic Games opener
item.description: Fiji has suffered a heavy 8-1 defeat to Senegal in its opening match of the U17 Futsal at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Senegal made a perfect start to its campaign, dominating the match to secure a convincing victory over the Fijian side.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji has suffered a heavy 8-1 defeat to Senegal in its opening match of the U17 Futsal at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

Senegal made a perfect start to its campaign, dominating the match to secure a convincing victory over the Fijian side.

Fiji will look to bounce back when it takes on Ukraine on Wednesday before facing Venezuela on Friday.

The team will be hoping to improve its performance and get its campaign back on track in its remaining pool matches.

item.title: Bulikula will back their style of footy ahead of Jillaroos semi-final clash - Coach
item.description: The Vodafone Bulikula have a style of footy they believe in, and the players remain committed to it, backing their skills and execution to finish tough games against any opposition. item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Bulikula have a style of footy they believe in, and the players remain committed to it, backing their skills and execution to finish tough games against any opposition.

Speaking from Australia, the Bulikula's defensive coach Isaac Michael expressed confidence in his players ahead of their clash against the Jillaroos in the Rugby League World Cup semi-final.

Michael says they will put together their best players to get the job done.

He says there are no major injuries in the team and the players are recovering well.

item.title: Arsenal beat Liverpool 1-0 to secure first Premier League win at Anfield since 2012
item.description: Arsenal have secured their first Premier League victory over Liverpool at Anfield since 2012 after defeating the home side 1-0. Kai Havertz scored the winning goal in the 16th minute following an assist from Declan Rice.
item.content:encoded:
Arsenal have secured their first Premier League victory over Liverpool at Anfield since 2012 after defeating the home side 1-0.

Kai Havertz scored the winning goal in the 16th minute following an assist from Declan Rice.

Arsenal took their one-goal lead into half-time and managed to hold on until the final whistle to secure all three points.

The victory marks an important comeback for the Gunners following their midweek defeat to League Two side Fleetwood.

The match also saw questions raised over whether Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty.

Despite the controversy, Arsenal held on to claim a historic away victory and end their long wait for a Premier League win at Anfield.

item.title: Khairati excited to begin professional football journey with Bula FC
item.description: 18-year-old Fijian international midfielder Abdullah Khairati says signing his first professional contract with Extra Bula FC is a dream come true after years of hard work towards becoming a professional footballer. Khairati, who was born in Vancouver, Canada, to a family of Fijian heritage, says he is grateful for the opportunity and is looking forward to making the most of it.
item.content:encoded:
18-year-old Fijian international midfielder Abdullah Khairati says signing his first professional contract with Extra Bula FC is a dream come true after years of hard work towards becoming a professional footballer.

Khairati, who was born in Vancouver, Canada, to a family of Fijian heritage, says he is grateful for the opportunity and is looking forward to making the most of it.

He says he has worked towards this moment for a long time and is thankful to the Almighty, his parents, coaches and everyone who has supported him throughout his journey.

Khairati says his parents have always believed in him, even during difficult times, and have reminded him to put God first, remain humble, patient, disciplined and grateful.

The midfielder, who has developed his football skills at Supra Academy since the age of 10, says he is determined to continue working hard and establish himself in the professional environment.

Describing himself as a hardworking, aggressive and tenacious midfielder, Khairati says he enjoys competing, winning back possession and helping his team control the game.

He says he is also looking forward to learning from experienced players in the Bula FC squad, including Fiji football star Roy Krishna and other Fiji internationals.

Khairati says playing alongside these established players will give him an opportunity to learn from their actions both on and off the pitch and gain as much knowledge as possible.

While he hopes to eventually play at the highest levels of European football, his immediate goals are to remain consistent, continue improving and score his first professional goal.

Khairati is also encouraging young Fijian footballers pursuing their dreams to believe in themselves, remain disciplined and never stop working towards their goals.

He says setbacks are part of the journey and young players must remain patient, continue improving, take every opportunity seriously and listen to their coaches.

Khairati says he is proud to join Bula FC and represent Fiji, adding that he is ready to give everything for the badge and contribute to the team in whatever way he can as he prepares for the 2027 OFC Professional League season.

Bula FC will begin their 2027 campaign in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, where they take on Tahiti United on the 22nd of January.
